howDoI.q: How do I make my hero fall down?
How do I let my hero jump and come back down?
How do I make a wall my hero has to jump over?
How do I turn gravity off?
How do I let my hero walk up and down as well as sideways?
How do I make a level that looks down from above?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Gravity On, Gravity Off is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels, and they are the same place twice. Level 1 shows it from the side, with gravity. Level 2 shows it from above, with gravity off. It takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

In level 1, Left and Right walk and Space jumps. In level 2, all four arrows walk, and Space does nothing. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on. Nothing in this game hurts Rima.

pages.head: Level 1: Gravity On
pages.html:
Level 1: Gravity On

Rima stands on the ground, and gravity pulls them down. The GRAVITY IS ON sign comes first: press Space and they lift up, then gravity brings them back to the ground where they started. The A WALL IS A STEP sign stands before a low brick wall. Walk into it and Rima is stopped. Jump and they clear it.

The ledge holds five coins, ten points each. Jump up onto it from the left, walk along it, and walk off the end: the WALK OFF THE LEDGE sign says what happens. Gravity pulls them straight down to the ground.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Gravity is a block setting. Open side.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the sky, the very first block. Under Gravity pulls, Down is checked. The engine looks at the block Rima is standing in, and if it pulls down they speed up toward the ground. Every blank block in the level, and the bushes, clouds, coins and signs, have the same tick, so they fall wherever they are in the air.
  • Solid blocks stop it. The ground, the wall and the ledge have Solid sides checked, so the pull stops when they land on one. The ledge has only its top side solid, so they can jump up through it from below.
  • Jumping. Open hero.chr in the character editor. The Jump sequence is one push upward, with Momentum on. The push carries them up, and gravity takes it back. Nothing in the engine says how high: the push and the pull do.
  • The wall. Two brick blocks stacked on the grass, with all four Solid sides checked. A jump rises a little over three blocks, so two is easy to clear.
  • Where it is. Open one.map in the map editor. The signs are a few ordinary blocks side by side, with words drawn in their pictures.
  • The exit. A scene link joins the door to the next level. Open grav.gam in the scenes editor.

What it cannot do. Gravity is for the hero only. Monsters are not pulled by it, and there is no one setting for a whole level: each block says it.

pages.head: Level 2: Gravity Off
pages.html:
Level 2: Gravity Off

The same place, from above. The wall is now a strip of stones along its top, the ledge a wooden deck, the bushes round shrubs. Rima is drawn from above too, facing whichever way they walk. The GRAVITY IS OFF sign comes first: all four arrows walk them, up and down as well as sideways.

The SPACE DOES NOTHING NOW sign stands before the wall. Press Space and nothing happens. Walk into the wall and they are stopped, so follow the path down, along and up to go around it. The deck holds the same five coins. Walk off its end and nothing pulls them down: it is only lawn.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • One setting. Open top.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the lawn, the first block. Under Gravity pulls, nothing is checked. In side.bbl the sky had Down checked. That tick is the whole difference between level 1 and level 2: with no pull, Rima stays where they are, and a key that moves them up or down just moves them.
  • The view is only pictures. Game-Maker has no top-down mode. The map is the same grid of blocks, and top.bbl draws each one as seen from above: the lawn, the stone wall top, the deck, the round shrubs. The wall is solid in both levels. The shrubs are solid only in this one, because their blocks have Solid sides checked here and not in side.bbl.
  • Walking up and down. Open top.chr. Up and Down are ordinary walking sequences, each moving Rima four pixels a frame, with a picture of their facing that way. In hero.chr the same two keys climb ladders and show them back. Left and Right are mirrored pictures of the same walk. Rima is one block tall here (their picture has only a bottom block), because from above there is no head over a body.
  • Space does nothing. top.chr gives no sequence the Space key, so pressing it changes nothing. A jump needs gravity to bring them back, and here there is none.
  • The wall to walk around. A column of wall blocks in two.map, with all four Solid sides checked. The path is only a picture of packed earth, so it leads the eye round the end of the wall.
  • The hedge. The whole map outside the room is hedge, with Solid sides checked, so Rima never stops at something they cannot see.
  • Which files each level uses. Open grav.gam in the scenes editor. Each level's scene lists its own block file and its own character file, which is how one game has a hero who climbs and a hero who walks.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In top.bbl, check Down under Gravity pulls for the lawn, and watch level 2 turn into a room Rima falls through.
  • In side.bbl, clear Down on the sky and see Rima float.
  • Check Up instead of Down on the sky, and they fall upward.
  • Check Right, and they are pushed along the ground.
  • Make the wall in one.map three blocks high, then four.
  • Move the coins somewhere harder to reach.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.back: A small explorer in a teal beanie visits the same place twice. First from the side, where gravity pulls them down and a wall is something to jump. Then from above, where nothing pulls their and the arrow keys walk their every way. Read the signs, then open the game in Game-Maker and change the Gravity of a block.
features: Level 1 is a side-scroller with gravity; level 2 is the same scene from above with gravity off
Rima walks in four directions when nothing pulls them down
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: The same little place, twice. In level 1 you see it from the side and gravity pulls Rima down: they jump a wall and walks off a ledge to fall. In level 2 you see it from above with gravity off, and Rima walks any of four ways and goes around the wall. Signs say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change one block's Gravity.

57.long: Jump in level 1, where gravity pulls you back down. In level 2 there is no gravity and Space does nothing.

72.long: Walk up in level 2, where gravity is off. Level 1 has no ladder.

80.long: Walk down in level 2, where gravity is off. Level 1 has no ladder.
